sections.name: File setup, Link, Item
sections.title: Imports, link and item types
sections.what: Brings in the PowerPoint library, the slide type, the shared colours, fonts and width, and the line estimator. It defines how a link is looked up for an item and what an item holds: its text and its position.
sections.why: Likely reason: shared imports keep body text drawn with the same design rules as the rest of the deck.
sections.watch_out: Only the imports and types are visible here, so the drawing behaviour cannot be checked from this section.

sections.name: height
sections.title: Estimating how tall text will be
sections.what: Estimates the height of a piece of text when it wraps inside a given width and font size, so the code can check it fits before drawing.
sections.why: Needed so the slide is never drawn with text that spills out of its box.
sections.watch_out: This is an estimate with a fixed adjustment factor, so very tight boxes can still overflow when rendered.

sections.name: renderCanonicalBody (part 1)
sections.title: Drawing the start of a fixed-format slide
sections.what: Works out one font size from the total text length, then defines the helpers that place each text item and draw divider lines. It also handles the row layout used by simpler profiles. If text does not fit, it throws an error instead of cutting text.
sections.why: Likely reason: fixed-format pages are built from stored text and must never silently lose or add items.
sections.watch_out: Because it throws on overflow rather than trimming, pagination must run first or the slide build will stop.

sections.name: renderCanonicalBody: if
sections.title: Choosing the layout for each slide type
sections.what: Picks a layout by profile: source and factbase slides use one or two numbered columns, framework and example slides use grid cards, project slides use a left panel with rows on the right, and other slides use plain rows.
sections.why: Likely reason: each kind of content reads best in a different arrangement.
sections.watch_out: The two-column split is chosen by searching for the most even break, so uneven text can give unbalanced columns, and an overflow error is thrown if a column runs past the page.

summary: Helper for drawing the main body text of a deck slide, taking the slide's text items and optional links.
purpose: Draws the body text of slides using the shared layout values.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Only the imports and types are visible in this packet.
how: Brings in the PowerPoint library, the slide type, the shared colours, fonts and width, and a line-count estimator. It defines a link lookup and a text item that carries its position in the list. The drawing steps are not visible in this packet.
inputs: Slide body items with text, and an optional link lookup for each item.
outputs: Body text placed on a PowerPoint slide. Exact outputs cannot be confirmed from this packet.
risks: Body text can overflow if the line estimate is wrong. Only part of the file is visible, so other risks cannot be judged.
debug: If body text overflows, check the line estimate from the pagination file and the text budget for the page. If links are missing, check that the link lookup returns a value for each item index.
